To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the core concept of institutionalism, the cultural embeddedness of human behavior and knowledge, is reaffirmed and that (2) the implications of this core concept for institutionalist inquiry have not been fully appreciated and implemented.

(1) The cultural approach is a useful and powerful way to study and explain human behavior, but it has been used in a variety of ways that are not all consistent with the core concept; (2) the cultural approach has been applied most consistently and productively in studies of the social construction of knowledge, and (3) the cultural approach can be applied more consistently in studies of other aspects of human behavior.
the two insights of institutional economics are not only compatible with each other but also with the insights of the natural sciences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the cultural nature of social science inquiry affects the nature and quality of social science knowledge and the efficacy of action guided by that knowledge.
the role of culture in economic life.
the role of culture in economic processes and the role of economic processes in culture, including the role of economics in economics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

culture, as a core concept of institutional economics, is the process by which humans, through their behavior and knowledge, create the conditions and circumstances that guide their behavior and knowledge.
the core concept of culture is a central insight in institutional economics.
institutionalism is not a single, unified, and coherent school.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while institutionalists are well aware of the importance of the cultural context, we have not been equally attentive to the cultural nature of inquiry and knowledge itself.
the institutionalist core concepts are reaffirmed but that they must be applied more consistently and more broadly.
institutionalists should be more explicit in their recognition that human inquiry is cultural and, therefore, subject to the same cultural processes and limitations as are the phenomena studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the core institutionalist insight that all human behavior is cultural has not been consistently applied, especially in the area of methodology, where it should be most obvious.
the institutionalist insights are robust. They are compatible with the natural sciences and are not threatened by the complications they introduce.
the institutionalist core concepts of culture and institutions must be reaffirmed and applied with greater rigor.
